meta.title: SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril & Onodrim | The Return of Conglomerates
meta.speakers: Christian Garrett (137 Ventures); host Molly O'Shea
meta.thread_line: 5 threads · SpaceX as hyperscaler · AI financing + pricing · growth portfolio + power law · return of the conglomerate · Onodrim + reindustrialization

snapshot: SpaceX is 137 Ventures' largest position after 16 years; Q3 top line grew about **160%** with $4.4B net income, and over half of revenue is now tied to AI.
Garrett sees SpaceX becoming a true hyperscaler with sub-12-month payback periods, and trading around 20-30x 2027 EBITDA as a **$2T** company.
Starship works: a handful of Starlink V3 satellites added about **1%** of the world's capacity, and orbital compute satellites are due in the back half of next year.
Debt markets now question AI build-out financing; cost of capital decides winners, and Elon is right that the strongest balance sheets win.
His thesis: the **return of the conglomerate**. Dual-use businesses like Palantir and SpaceX, with majority commercial revenue, are the model for defense.
He co-founded **Onodrim** to buy and scale European aerospace and defense suppliers, the layer below 4,000 overfunded drone startups.

themes.title: SpaceX turns into a vertically integrated hyperscaler
themes.lead: Garrett calls SpaceX the most important company in the world, now monetizing AI from the app layer down to compute.
bullets: Q3: top line up about **160%**, $4.4B net income, roughly $8.8-10B EBITDA; over 50% of revenue is attributed to AI.
AI revenue from Cursor and Grokbots; it builds compute capacity fastest and either uses it or sells it, with sub-12-month payback periods.
Vertical integration hedges the model mix: it wins whether open source or closed models win, and can shift capacity to its own products if demand slows.
Starship is working; a handful of Starlink V3s added about **1%** of the world's capacity, and tens of thousands are coming.
Orbital compute satellites are slated for the back half of next year; Google tested a version in orbit, and StarCloud 3 will fly on Starship.
It compounded about **40% for 20 years**; duration is what matters (9% over 30 years is 13x). It trades at 20-30x 2027 EBITDA as a $2T company.
Cheaper launch built companies like Varda (pharma, defense); Starship should cut costs by an order of magnitude and spawn as many new firms.

themes.title: AI build-out financing and the cost-of-capital edge
themes.lead: Markets now doubt both who funds the spend and who pays for it, and Garrett says pricing anything means believing in out-year earnings nobody can see.
bullets: Volatility in public and debt markets: macro, an election cycle and October de-grossing all play a role, and both spenders and beneficiaries of the spend dropped.
Speed, payback period and **cost of capital** decide the build-out, since debt is the most efficient funding; CoreWeave-type names felt it first.
Elon's tweet on financing constraints is 100% right: low-cost-of-capital players will absorb supply at better rates.
Unknowns: model pricing, open versus closed mix, compute pricing, power access. It's hard to believe the next two years of earnings, let alone 20.
Bets at the harness and app layers: **Cognition**, plus a co-led round in Hex for data workflows; he expects open source to take a large share of models.
OpenAI and Anthropic are two of the most impressive businesses built in a generation; family members using chatbots signal early diffusion.

themes.title: Paying up for winners: the growth-stage power law
themes.lead: Too much capital chases too few growth companies, but the power law still pays for it.
bullets: Molly: Cognition was at **$48B** and is rumored at $60-70B, Ramp at $60B, Anduril at $90B; Shardul (Index) will pay a 25% premium but not 2x.
Teddy Forstmann, Garrett's godfather: own a quality 5x asset at a 25% premium over a bad one at a 25% discount.
Ramp keeps consolidating the back office and is still underpriced and under-monetized on several products.
The COVID fintech flood left most companies dead, but Stripe, Revolut and Nubank became $100B-plus outcomes; he expects the same in AI and defense.
Growth portfolios behave like venture: a handful of companies drive all the returns.

quote.text: Just a handful of companies drive all the returns.

themes.title: The return of the dual-use conglomerate
themes.lead: New conglomerates share one tech platform, unlike the disparate 1980s versions, and defense needs commercial scale to stay affordable.
bullets: Old conglomerates offered diversification and cost-of-capital scale, but had no shared platform, made sum-of-the-parts hard, and suffered diseconomies.
New ones share a core operating platform and vertical integration (Apple, SpaceX); Anduril's Lattice means every product sold raises the value of the others.
**Palantir** and SpaceX get the majority of revenue from the commercial sector; China's defense primes get about 68% from commercial; General Mills once made cereal and weapon systems.
Industrial policy can't fund defense capacity alone; you must dominate commercially, as China's shipbuilding prime does. He expects Anduril to be by far the power outcome among neo-primes.
Anduril bringing computer manufacturing home is part of repatriating capacity, which Palmer Luckey pushed for years.

themes.title: Onodrim: rolling up Europe's defense supplier layer
themes.lead: Garrett co-founded a platform to buy, modernize and scale the fragmented European suppliers below the primes.
bullets: US models like TransDigm, Teledyne, HEICO and Honeywell consolidated suppliers; Europe never had a HEICO, despite a mature Airbus supply chain.
Europe has **4,000 drone companies** (overfunded) while engines, components and structures, the layer below, are the production bottleneck.
It acquires and holds long term, funds capex and new products, deploys technology into manufacturing, and targets dual-use firms. First acquisitions and prime partnerships are coming soon.
The team spans private equity, defense, government, Palantir and SpaceX, with nine nationalities; he is a minority co-founder.
Like Armada (incubated from a SpaceX idea), it started from a problem he was close to. Also bullish on Hadrian, AI integrating into PLCs, Applied Intuition and General Matter (uranium enrichment).

takeaways.title: Value SpaceX on its hyperscaler payback and duration of growth, not on launch alone.
Screen AI infrastructure names by cost of capital; cheap money wins the build-out.
Look below the neo-primes: component and supplier capacity is the bottleneck.
Favor dual-use businesses whose commercial scale subsidizes defense capacity.

other_news.title: Garrett warns against political weaponization of tech, from Tesla cars being burned to boycotts of Anthropic: judge companies on their merits, and the market sorts the rest.
He calls tech uniquely non-zero-sum, partly because it grows and partly by culture, and is saddened by petty infighting.
